title: Certificates
description: Manage ACME HTTPS site certificates and renewal. Background work runs on the server.
caSeparation: Site certificates are separate from Gateway MITM CA and TLS Auto private CA. Private keys are never displayed.
name: Name
stagingHelp: Use Staging to test challenges. Staging certificates are not publicly trusted; choose Production for a public HTTPS site.
httpHelp: Enable ACME HTTP-01 on an existing plain HTTP Gateway listening on port 80. Public DNS must reach it, and its source ACL must allow CA validators. No new listener is opened automatically. Wildcards require DNS-01.
dnsHelp: DNS-01 requires API write access to the authoritative zone. Supports wildcards. TXT propagation is checked and only this task’s records are removed.
terms: I accept the selected ACME CA’s terms of service
privateTrust: Private CA trust (public PEM roots only)
privateTrustHelp: For a custom private CA, provide public root certificates. This does not change DNS provider trust. HTTPS verification remains enabled.
identityEditHelp: Remove listener references before changing domains, or issue a new certificate and replace the reference.
tokenHelp: Use a token with DNS record read/write access limited to this zone. It is stored privately and never returned.
keepToken: Leave blank to keep the existing token.
deleteWarning: Delete “{{name}}”? Referenced certificates and providers still used by a certificate or cleanup task cannot be deleted.
referenceHelp: Select one or more site certificates. New TLS handshakes use the latest verified pair and must match SNI. Pending or expired resources fail closed.
unavailable: Could not load certificates. Check permissions and connection.
expiryWarning: Certificate expires within 14 days or has expired. Check renewal and listener readiness.
failure_ca_rate_limited: The CA rate limit was reached. Wait until the next scheduled attempt.
failure_acme_request_failed: The CA request or certificate validation failed. Check the CA URL, challenge access and trust roots.
failure_dns_provider_unavailable: DNS provider credentials are missing or unavailable.
failure_dns_zone_mismatch: A requested domain is outside the configured DNS zone.
failure_dns_propagation_timeout: The TXT proof did not propagate before timeout.
failure_dns_rate_limited: The DNS provider rate limit was reached.
failure_dns_api_rejected: The DNS provider rejected the request. Check token permissions and zone ID.
failure_dns_network_error: The DNS provider could not be reached over verified HTTPS.
failure_dns_challenge_failed: DNS challenge setup or cleanup failed. Check the provider and recent events.
managementBindingHelp: First issue a valid certificate, then add this argument to the installed service and restart it. Use its DNS name to connect. Existing self-signed and file modes remain the default until you explicitly change the service.
managementBindingSafety: Do not combine with certificate/key file or generated-name arguments. Missing or expired material stops startup; there is no plaintext fallback. Renewal then applies automatically. To return to the original mode, remove this argument and restart.
managementRestoredHelp: For a deployment that adopted restored startup inputs, review -recovery-startup=false before changing host TLS settings.
ari_available: The CA suggested this renewal window. The backend schedules renewal with jitter and checks again at the recorded time.
ari_unsupported: ARI is not advertised or this certificate cannot use it. Renewal uses the certificate lifetime.
ari_unavailable: CA advice could not be refreshed. The current renewal plan and valid certificate are retained; metadata retries do not reset issuance backoff.
ari_unknown: CA renewal advice has not been confirmed.
